## Summary

[Partial] Torque front and rear shock bolts using specified values with anti-seize or compression aid. [t1045]

[Partial] [Unverified value] Torque front shock top nut between 12-16 ft-lbs and adjust with a 7mm allen socket. [t1045]

[Partial] [Unverified value] Torque the rear shock bottom fitting to a range of 30-37 ft-lbs. [t1045]

[Unverified value] Torqes the rear wheel lug nuts to 80 ft-lbs. [t1045]

Locate the K&N Filter RX-4750 featuring an oval tapered universal style with a centered flange. [t1090]

[Partial] Rear leaf springs are 2-3/8 inches wide. [t1941]

Chevrolet C10 springs are 2.5 inches wide. [t1941]

[Partial] Use a stock Xterra rear spring pack providing roughly 3-3/4 inches of lift with SOA. [t1941]

Expect 5+ inches of lift when combining new leaf springs with SOA and stock shackles. [t1941]

[Partial] Use a 72-inch C10 spring from a local junkyard as an affordable option. [t1941]

Note that the stock manifold often features an integral primary cat bolted directly to it. [t1917]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use anti-seize or WD40 on bolts to aid installation. [t1045]
- [Partial] Compress the shock slightly before lining up the bottom fitting. [t1045]
- Use the 7mm allen socket on the Bilstein shock head for adjustment. [t1045]
- Tighten until bushings are slightly compressed if a torque wrench is hard to fit. [t1045]
- The filter features an oval tapered universal style with a centered flange type. [t1090]
- [Partial] Rear leaf springs are 2-3/8 inches wide. [t1941]
- Chevrolet C10 springs are 2.5 inches wide. [t1941]
- A stock Xterra rear spring pack provides roughly 3-3/4 inches of lift when using SOA. [t1941]
- Expect 5+ inches of lift when combining new leaf springs with SOA and stock shackles. [t1941]
- [Partial] A 72-inch C10 spring from a local junkyard is an affordable option. [t1941]
- Inspect old bolts before reusing to prevent yielding or breaking off inside the manifold. [t1326]
- [Partial] Use a 6-rib balancer and AC pulley for optimal ratios, especially if upgrading to solid couplers. [t1326]
- [Partial] Verify headers were torqued down correctly if misfires persist after other repairs. [t1316]
- Note that improper head gasket repair can lead to minor coolant leaks before major failure. [t1316]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a shallow 18mm socket that didn't bite well, leading to potential slippage if not torqued carefully. [t1045]
